messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

message.reasoning:
We need to call two functions:

1. Celebrity net worth get for Lionel Messi in Euro.

But we have only one function "celebrity_net_worth_get". It takes parameters: name:string, currency:string. So we can pass name="Lionel Messi", currency="EUR".

Similarly second request: net worth of LeBron James in GBP -> name="LeBron James", currency="GBP"

Third: BMI calculation with weight=85 kg height=180 cm unit='metric'.

Fourth: BMI calculation with weight=200 lbs height=6 ft 2 in; but our BMI calculator expects weight in kilograms and height in centimeters if unit unspecified or maybe it accepts both units? Let's check description: "Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person." Parameters: weight:number, height:number, optional unit default 'metric'. If unit is 'imperial', presumably weight should be in pounds and height in inches. But they gave weight=200 pounds and height=6ft 2in. We need convert to numeric values: weight=200, height=? For imperial, height likely given as inches. 6 ft 2 in equals 74 inches. So we set weight=200, height=74, unit='imperial'.

Thus calls:

First function: celebrity_net_worth_get({name:"Lionel Messi", currency:"EUR"}) -> returns value.

Second: celebrity_net_worth_get({name:"LeBron James", currency:"GBP"}).

Third: calculate_bmi({weight:85,height:180,unit:'metric'}). Actually unit param may not needed because default metric. Provide anyway.

Fourth: calculate_bmi({weight:200,height:74,unit:'imperial'}).

We'll produce JSON responses accordingly. Use tool invocation format exactly. We'll output each result separately. Probably best to do sequentially.
